native_method: tools.view_image of exact full JPEGs; full canvases used for localisation only, then nominated plant/complete row anatomy and label geometry; no crop/image edit generated
coordinate_convention: approximate manually localized [left,top,right,bottom] native-pixel bounding boxes; these are reviewed regions, not generated crop files or exact contours

features: One continuous upright central green stem rises from large orange-brown swollen tapering root with fine lateral root hairs.
Several long arched/lax side axes carry separate pointed triangular or arrow-like green blades with basal notches and some irregular lobes.
Multiple hanging clusters of small circular outlined bodies with red centres occur at ends of the lateral axes. These are fruit-like drawing structures, not an identified species.
Root broadens below stem and tapers sideways to a point; body is mostly a smooth outlined mass with drawn internal strokes and fine protruding fibres.
herbal_anatomy.limits: No species identification, organ translation, glyph reading, or botanical life-cycle claim. Whole depicted anatomy does not prove a botanically exhaustive plant.

limits: Historical development nominations are not independent holdouts.
Source-nominated identity is a hypothesis, not ground truth.
No ROOT, q, Part operator, species, process or extraction translation.
No GDT388 gate or reserved-confirmation claim.
Whole-canvas incidental areas and visible glyphs are exposure only, not interpreted.

source_nominated_pair.locator: top row fragment116, five plants/six labels

pharma_anatomy.anatomy: A slender orange/brown axis makes a conspicuous closed coil/spiral, with several separately attached pointed triangular/arrow-like green leaves and thin tapering lower extensions/root-like tips. No red-centred clusters or large swollen root are visible.
pharma_anatomy.coidentity_rival: Best local leaf/axis resemblance to herbal hypothesis, but coil, tiny root and absence of clusters are substantial counterfeatures.

distinctive_concordance: Separately attached pointed triangular/basal-notched leaf silhouettes and a slender curved axis resemble part of the herbal drawing.
counter_features: Top second plant coils into a tight loop/spiral; herbal side axes arch but do not show this closed main coil.
Large swollen hairy root and repeated red-centred hanging clusters of herbal plant are absent from the nominated top second drawing.
Leaves are fewer and some much narrower; relative spacing/branch architecture differs.
Other top-row plants also have pointed/lobed green foliar forms, so leaf shape alone is not a singular identity cue.

continuity_or_cut.observed: Leaf attachments and brown coiled axis are continuous. Narrow lower tips curve/taper; none is an independently visible severed cross-section.

simplification_rival: Smaller juvenile/abbreviated/stylized whole-plant rendering or leaf-family resemblance can explain absent root mass/red clusters. Those rival descriptions are possible drawing accounts, not identified biological stages.
